lessons.concept_md: Python programs can write text to standard output with `print()`.
lessons.hidden_hint: Only the text inside the quotes needs to change.
lessons.prompt: Change the program so it prints `Hello, Padawan!` exactly.
lessons.title: Hello Python

lessons.codex_context: Use A Variable lesson for Padawan.
lessons.concept_md: A variable gives a value a name. An f-string can place that value into output with `{name}`.
lessons.hidden_hint: Only the value assigned to `name` needs to change.
lessons.prompt: Update the variable so the program prints `Hello, Padawan!`.
lessons.title: Use A Variable

lessons.codex_context: Choose With If lesson for Padawan.
lessons.concept_md: `if` lets a program choose a path. Comparisons such as `>=` produce true or false.
lessons.hidden_hint: The score should pass when it is at least three.
lessons.prompt: Update the condition so this program prints `ready`.
lessons.title: Choose With If

lessons.codex_context: Return A Value lesson for Padawan.
lessons.concept_md: A function packages reusable behavior. `return` sends a value back to the caller.
lessons.hidden_hint: The function should multiply the input by two.
lessons.title: Return A Value
